elements.element: Customer owns every deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Customer owns only Materials designated Type I. Materials created during the Services may be designated or default to Type II and remain owned by IBM or third parties.

elements.element: Customer owns every item of work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause does not allocate all work product to Customer and does not use or define a comprehensive work-product category.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no operative assignment by IBM; the clause merely states that Customer will have rights in designated Type I Materials.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment obligation covering work product appears.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Type I is limited to Materials created during Service performance, while Type II expressly includes pre-existing Materials and leaves title with IBM or applicable third parties.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor intellectual property embedded in deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence covers copies of specified Type II Materials, not all IBM intellectual property embedded in Type I or other deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Although the Type II licence is perpetual, no licence covering all embedded Vendor IP is granted.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Although the Type II licence is irrevocable, no licence covering all embedded Vendor IP is granted.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Although the Type II licence is royalty-free, no licence covering all embedded Vendor IP is granted.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The redline limits IBM's licence and processing purposes but does not affirmatively provide that Customer retains all right, title, and interest in all Customer Data.

elements.element: There is no joint ownership between Customer and Vendor.
elements.evidence: Type I Materials are allocated entirely to Customer, while Type II Materials are allocated entirely to IBM or third parties; no Customer-IBM joint ownership is created.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: Generic tools are not expressly reserved to IBM. A tool created during the Services could be designated Type I and become Customer-owned under the clause.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: Know-how is not mentioned or reserved, and the broad grant of all right, title, and interest in Type I Materials contains no know-how carve-out.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence covering Vendor-owned deliverables.
elements.evidence: IBM grants Customer a licence to copies of Type II Materials, the category owned by IBM or third parties; Customer has the stronger right of ownership in Type I Materials.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor-owned deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor-owned deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor-owned deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence is expressly worldwide.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor-owned deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence expressly permits use.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence expressly permits modification.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence expressly permits sublicensing.

elements.element: The licensed rights may be exercised for Customer's business.
elements.evidence: The Type II licence applies for Customer's business purposes.

result.reason: The redline successfully adds the fallback licence's duration, geographic scope, economic terms, and use, modification, and sublicensing rights. It does not, however, reserve generic tools and know-how categorically to IBM, so the complete fallback is not met. The preferred position also fails because Customer ownership is limited to designated Type I Materials, no assignment is given, embedded IBM IP is not comprehensively licensed, and Customer's ownership of Customer Data is not stated. The edits remain coherent and preserve the Type I/Type II structure, but they are not minimal to a complete level because neither level is fully achieved and the data-use edits go beyond what is needed for the otherwise nearly complete fallback.
